intro.title: useId & Stable IDs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with multiple input fields, each requiring a unique ID for accessibility. You will learn the core concept of generating stable, unique identifiers across server and client renders to prevent hydration mismatches. The main technology involved is React's built-in useId Hook, which provides a simple way to create these IDs. By the end, you'll understand why useId is better than manual counters or random strings for generating IDs in React components.
intro.usecase: In real applications, stable IDs are essential for connecting form labels to their inputs for accessibility, linking ARIA attributes in complex UI components, and ensuring consistent server-client rendering. Developers encounter this when building accessible form libraries, dynamic data tables with expandable rows, or multi-step wizards where elements need persistent identifiers. For example, in a dashboard with collapsible panels or a settings page with toggle switches, useId ensures screen readers can properly announce state changes and users can navigate via keyboard without ID collisions during re-renders.
